title: Creating Sashimi-Style Plots with spliceTerrain
text: Sashimi plots visualise RNA-seq alignments across genomic interval. combine per-base read coverage arcs representing reads span splice junctions. makes useful inspecting transcript structure, exon usage, alternative splice sites, intron retention, differences junction usage samples.

title: Creating Sashimi-Style Plots with spliceTerrain
text: Several excellent tools already exist generating sashimi-style visualisations, including genome browsers, command-line tools, workflow-specific plotting utilities. spliceTerrain intended complement approaches providing R-native interface works naturally within Bioconductor ecosystem reproducible analysis documents. many RNA-seq analyses, regions interest, annotations, genomic features already represented GRanges GRangesList objects. spliceTerrain accepts objects directly, making straightforward move differential splicing result genomic annotation sashimi plot inside R session. users want control, processed coverage junction data can also returned, inspected, modified, replotted.

title: Creating Sashimi-Style Plots with spliceTerrain
text: bam argument character vector indexed BAM file paths. vector named, names used sample labels plot. unnamed, labels derived BAM file names. BAM files must indexed region-restricted import. Index files discoverable Rsamtools using standard -directory naming, typically file.bam.bai. region argument can character string, GRanges, GRangesList. Character regions may use comma-separated coordinates, "chr14:70,233,810-70,238,690". Bioconductor workflows, using GRanges object often convenient. example BAM files use UCSC style chromosome names, also convert region UCSC style plotting. multiple ranges supplied, spliceTerrain() reduces single span one chromosome uses span BAM query plotting window. span smallest continuous interval containing supplied ranges: starts lowest start coordinate ends highest end coordinate.
code: bams <- RNAseqData.HNRNPC.bam.chr14_BAMFILES[c(7, 1)] names(bams) <- c("HNRNPC knockdown", "Control") ensDb <- EnsDb.Hsapiens.v75 region <- transcripts(ensDb, filter = TxIdFilter("ENST00000394366")) seqlevelsStyle(region) <- "UCSC" region #> GRanges object with 1 range and 6 metadata columns: #>                   seqnames            ranges strand |           tx_id     tx_biotype tx_cds_seq_start tx_cds_seq_end         gene_id         tx_name #>                      <Rle>         <IRanges>  <Rle> |     <character>    <character>        <integer>      <integer>     <character>     <character> #>   ENST00000394366    chr14 70233810-70238690      + | ENST00000394366 protein_coding         70234874       70238178 ENSG00000100650 ENST00000394366 #>   ------- #>   seqinfo: 1 sequence from hg19 genome

title: Creating Sashimi-Style Plots with spliceTerrain
text: Transcript models can displayed annotation argument. must GRangesList, list element represents one transcript feature group. names list elements used y-axis labels annotation panel. annotation present, final plot contains one panel per BAM file plus one annotation panel. relative heights panels controlled panel_heights, final value corresponds annotation panel. vignette, plotting region covers SRSF5 gene. retrieve exon ranges gene keep small number transcripts annotation panel remains readable.
code: annotation <- exonsBy(     ensDb, by = "tx", filter = GeneIdFilter("ENSG00000100650") ) annotation <- annotation[1:3] seqlevelsStyle(annotation) <- "UCSC" spliceTerrain(     bam = bams,     region = region,     annotation = annotation,     panel_heights = c(2, 2, 1) )

title: Creating Sashimi-Style Plots with spliceTerrain
text: Annotation features can coloured metadata column anno_fill_by. Use "group" colour transcript feature group separately. Specific fill colours can supplied anno_fill_colours. Text labels can drawn inside annotation features anno_label_by. label colour size controlled anno_label_colour anno_label_size. min_arrow argument controls wide annotation intron must directional arrows drawn.
code: spliceTerrain(     bam = bams,     region = region,     annotation = annotation,     panel_heights = c(2, 2, 1),     anno_fill_by = "group",     anno_fill_colours = c(         ENST00000553369 = "#66C2A5",         ENST00000394366 = "#8DA0CB",         ENST00000451983 = "#FC8D62"     ),     anno_label_by = "exon_rank",     anno_label_colour = "black",     anno_label_size = 2.5,     min_arrow = 100 )

title: Creating Sashimi-Style Plots with spliceTerrain
text: highlight argument marks one genomic intervals shaded vertical bands. useful drawing attention splice site, variant position, alternative exon, feature interest. highlighted interval can supplied character string GRanges object.  wider interval can highlighted semi-transparent colour.
code: spliceTerrain(     bam = bams,     region = region,     highlight = "chr14:70234854-70234854",     highlight_colour = "red" ) spliceTerrain(     bam = bams,     region = region,     highlight = "chr14:70234056-70234097",     highlight_colour = scales::alpha("red", 0.2) )

title: Creating Sashimi-Style Plots with spliceTerrain
text: Percent spliced (PSI) commonly used summarise often splice choice used relative local splice choices. spliceTerrain(), psi argument identifies local genomic interval labels junctions whose start end anchor overlaps interval. Junction anchors use intronic coordinates: start anchor first base intron, end anchor last base intron, adjacent exonic bases. label reports selected junction’s fraction included junction reads. intended interpretable local junction-usage label sashimi plot, rather full transcript-level isoform inference.
code: spliceTerrain(     bam = bams,     region = region,     psi = "chr14:70234854-70234854" )

title: Creating Sashimi-Style Plots with spliceTerrain
text: Three arguments control much signal imported displayed. min_mapq filters alignments mapping quality BAM import. min_coverage filters per-base coverage positions plotting. min_junction_reads filters splice junction arcs supporting read count.  Technical note: min_coverage min_junction_reads applied raw counts library-size normalisation applied.
code: spliceTerrain(     bam = bams,     region = region,     min_mapq = 10,     min_coverage = 10,     min_junction_reads = 20 )

title: Creating Sashimi-Style Plots with spliceTerrain
text: strandedness argument describes read strand interpreted. can one "unstranded", "forward", "reverse", can supplied either single value BAM files one value per BAM file. example BAM files unstranded, read orientations contain signal transcript.  Specifying stranded protocol unstranded BAM files filters reads strand. result, either "reverse" "forward" shows part coverage visible strandedness = "unstranded".   paired-end BAM files, spliceTerrain() detects paired-end status BAM alignment flags imports alignments accordingly. region specifies strand strandedness "unstranded", alignments restricted resolved region strand.
code: spliceTerrain(     bam = bams,     region = region,     strandedness = "unstranded" ) spliceTerrain(     bam = bams,     region = region,     strandedness = "forward" ) spliceTerrain(     bam = bams,     region = region,     strandedness = "reverse" )

title: Creating Sashimi-Style Plots with spliceTerrain
text: samples different sequencing depths, coverage junction counts can normalised lib_size. Additional normalisation factors, edgeR TMM factors, can supplied norm_factors. effective library size calculated lib_size * norm_factors. default, counts normalised median effective library size. Use normalise_to set target explicitly. common_y argument useful comparing samples puts sample panels y-axis scale.
code: spliceTerrain(     bam = bams,     region = region,     lib_size = c(40e6, 55e6),     norm_factors = c(0.95, 1.08),     normalise_to = 50e6,     common_y = TRUE )

title: Creating Sashimi-Style Plots with spliceTerrain
text: default, compress_introns = TRUE compacts large uninformative gaps plot focuses observed signal. intron_width argument controls approximate width compacted introns plot space.  exact genomic distances important compact display, intron compression can disabled.
code: spliceTerrain(     bam = bams,     region = region,     compress_introns = TRUE,     intron_width = 500 ) spliceTerrain(     bam = bams,     region = region,     compress_introns = FALSE )

title: Creating Sashimi-Style Plots with spliceTerrain
text: Junction arcs can tuned arc_height, arc_side, arc_scale. Increasing arc_height gives stacked arcs vertical separation. arc_side argument controls whether arcs drawn , , sides coverage track. arc_scale = TRUE, arc line width scaled junction read count filtering. Junction label size controlled junc_text_size.
code: spliceTerrain(     bam = bams,     region = region,     psi = "chr14:70234854-70234854",     arc_height = 2,     arc_side = "above",     arc_scale = TRUE,     junc_text_size = 2.5 )

title: Creating Sashimi-Style Plots with spliceTerrain
text: colours argument controls colours used sample coverage junction arcs. can single colour used samples one colour per BAM file. Axis text sizes can adjusted axis_title_size axis_text_size.
code: spliceTerrain(     bam = bams,     region = region,     annotation = annotation,     colours = c("darkblue", "darkred"),     panel_heights = c(2, 2, 1),     axis_title_size = 20,     axis_text_size = 12 )

title: Creating Sashimi-Style Plots with spliceTerrain
text: users can work directly final plot returned spliceTerrain(). advanced workflows, set return_ctx = TRUE return processed context instead. contains validated inputs, imported alignments, summarised coverage, junction counts, mapped plot-space data, plot settings. context can passed back ctx argument redraw plot without re-importing BAM files recalculating coverage junctions.
code: ctx <- spliceTerrain(     bam = bams,     region = region,     return_ctx = TRUE )  names(ctx) #> [1] "input" "plot" names(ctx$plot) #> [1] "cov"        "juncs"      "map"        "annotation" "region"     "psi"        "highlight"  "plist" spliceTerrain(ctx = ctx)

May GRanges, GRangesList, character string coercible GRanges, "chr:start-end" "chr:start-end:strand". Commas, spaces, en/em dashes character regions normalised coercion. multiple ranges supplied, must seqname reduced single span used BAM query plotting window. annotation Optional annotation track. Must GRangesList, list element representing one feature group transcript model. group drawn annotation row. List element names used y-axis labels; absent, default group labels generated. Annotation groups retained overlap plotting region clipped plotting window drawn. psi Optional genomic interval used annotate junction labels local junction usage (percent spliced , PSI). Accepts formats region. Junctions start end anchor overlapping psi labelled fraction total junction reads among selected junctions. psi_label_sep Character scalar inserted junction counts PSI percentages junction labels psi supplied. Defaults "\n"; use " " keep percentages inline counts. highlight Optional interval(s) highlight. Accepts formats region. Multiple ranges may supplied. Highlighted intervals drawn shaded vertical bands spanning full panel height. strandedness Library strandedness BAM. Must one "unstranded", "forward", "reverse", may supplied either single value applied BAMs one value per BAM. Use "unstranded" reads strands included. stranded paired-end BAMs, value passed readGAlignmentPairs strandMode. region includes strand strandedness "unstranded", imported alignments restricted overlaps resolved region strand. min_mapq Integer scalar. Minimum mapping quality (MAPQ) alignments imported BAM file. min_coverage Integer scalar integer vector. Minimum per-base coverage required positions retained plotting. May supplied either single value applied BAMs one value per BAM. min_junction_reads Integer scalar integer vector. Minimum number split reads supporting junction retained plotting. May supplied either single value applied BAMs one value per BAM. lib_size Optional numeric vector giving RNA-seq library sizes, one per BAM file. supplied, coverage junction counts normalised effective library size plotting. norm_factors Optional numeric vector normalisation factors, one per BAM file, edgeR TMM normalisation factors. Requires lib_size. Effective library sizes calculated lib_size * norm_factors. normalise_to Optional numeric scalar giving target library size used normalisation. NULL, counts normalised median effective library size. compress_introns Logical scalar. Passed ggplot2::geom_label() junction annotations. panel_heights Numeric vector controlling relative heights plot panels. Must length 1 number BAM sample panels plus one additional value annotation panel shown. annotation panel shown, height specified final value. axis_title_size Numeric scalar giving axis title text size used final plot theme. axis_text_size Numeric scalar giving axis tick-label text size used final plot theme. return_ctx Logical scalar. code: if (   requireNamespace("RNAseqData.HNRNPC.bam.chr14", quietly = TRUE) &&   requireNamespace("EnsDb.Hsapiens.v75", quietly = TRUE) &&   requireNamespace("AnnotationFilter", quietly = TRUE) &&   requireNamespace("ensembldb", quietly = TRUE) ) {   bams <- RNAseqData.HNRNPC.bam.chr14::RNAseqData.HNRNPC.bam.chr14_BAMFILES   bams <- bams[c(7, 1)]   names(bams) <- c("HNRNPC knockdown", "Control")   region <- "chr14:70,233,810-70,238,690"    annotation <- ensembldb::exonsBy(     EnsDb.Hsapiens.v75::EnsDb.Hsapiens.v75,     by = "tx",     filter = AnnotationFilter::GeneIdFilter("ENSG00000100650")   )   annotation <- annotation[1:3]   ensembldb::seqlevelsStyle(annotation) <- "ucsc"    spliceTerrain(bam = bams, region = region)    spliceTerrain(     bam = bams,     region = region,     lib_size = c(40e6, 55e6),     norm_factors = c(0.95, 1.08),     common_y = TRUE   )    spliceTerrain(     bam = bams,     region = region,     annotation = annotation,     anno_fill_by = "group",     anno_fill_colours = c(         ENST00000553369 = "#66C2A5",         ENST00000394366 = "#8DA0CB",         ENST00000451983 = "#FC8D62"     ),     anno_label_by = "exon_rank",     anno_label_colour = "black",     psi = "chr14:70234854-70234854",     highlight = "chr14:70233810-70234097",     arc_height = 2,     arc_side = "above",     arc_scale = TRUE,     common_y = TRUE,     colours = c("darkblue", "darkred"),     highlight_colour = scales::alpha("gold", 0.25),     anno_label_size = 2,     panel_heights = c(2, 2, 1)   )    ctx <- spliceTerrain(     bam = bams,     region = region,     annotation = annotation,     min_junction_reads = 1,     panel_heights = c(2, 2, 1),     return_ctx = TRUE   )   ctx$plot$juncs <- ctx$plot$juncs[ctx$plot$juncs$coverage >= 20]   spliceTerrain(ctx = ctx) }
